blocks.body:
# Client Enrollment Requirements Audit — 4 August 2026

Firebase-backed review of the old and current guard enrollment setup for all clients.

## The enrollment setup now preserves every verified client-specific requirement

All **15 current clients** now have explicit enrollment profiles: **13 standard**, **1 TCS**, and **1 LNG Petronet**. The LNG flow again collects service-book and arms-licence uploads by applicable designation, exposes both sections for optional collection when not mandatory, and restores the missing bank-branch and PAN-document requirements. TCS continues to require its resource ID.

## LNG history confirms a broad core form plus designation-specific documents

The historical LNG cohort contains near-universal designation, PAN, nationality, identification-mark, height, weight, and bank-branch data. Service-book documents appear in **151 of 166 records** because they apply to ex-service, supervisor, and armed-guard roles—not to every designation. The restored form keeps this distinction while making the upload section discoverable for all LNG applicants.

## Three explicit profiles replace fragile name-only behavior

Each client now stores its enrollment profile and requirements in Firebase. The frontend receives that profile from the public client endpoint, and both public and administrator enrollment forms use the same normalized configuration resolver. A client override can now enable a field even when the global default disables it.

## Service book and arms licence are conditional, not globally mandatory

Historical designation coverage shows that service-book uploads belong to ex-service, supervisor, and armed-guard enrollment. Arms-licence details belong only to armed guards. The backend now enforces these conditions, while the frontend explains when each section is optional or required.

## The comparison used configuration, source forms, and historical field presence

The audit enumerated every client record, inspected the legacy LNG import schema, reviewed historical employee-field presence by client and designation, and compared those requirements with both current enrollment screens and backend validation. Only aggregate counts were retained in this report. The production database repair backed up each affected document before writing explicit client profiles and global overrides.

## Historical presence establishes applicability, not perfect completion

A missing value in an old employee record can mean the document was optional, not applicable, or never completed. Therefore the audit inferred conditional requirements only where designation patterns and the legacy form agreed. Standard clients retain the common enrollment profile because Firebase history did not establish additional client-specific fields for them.

## Recommended operating checks

1. Add a client-profile review whenever a new client is created.
2. Keep the profile-repair script available as a dry-run audit before future configuration migrations.
3. Monitor enrollment validation failures by client and field so missing requirements are detected before guards are blocked.
4. Preserve frontend, backend, and Firebase configuration parity in every enrollment release.

### Further questions

No further requirement gap is evident from the current Firebase client and historical enrollment data. Re-audit when a client requests a new contractual document or employee attribute.
